assets.defect_engineered: 105x148mm A6 card whose CITY/VENUE/ADDRESS/DATE/HOST_NAME/HOST_TITLE/SEAT_TIER/STANDING_LINE are ONE continuous text story in ONE frame (no per-field frames); the mapping readout SILENTLY DROPS the SEAT_TIER run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short and the STANDING_LINE never lands while the validator returns VALID and prepare reports success; genuine picture well (per-row venue photo binds) but a fixed one-line venue measure that TRUNCATES long venue names at the trim edge; NO bleed box (media box = trim)
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for norvant_launch_card_2025.pdf — last year's regional event card, exactly as it went to the printer (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered into a live InDesign merge template downstream).

Document: 105 x 148 mm PORTRAIT (A6), single card, fonts embedded (a plain neutral grotesque for the detail lines and a measured serif companion for the city heading — the printer's own faces, not the announcement-set type). NO bleed box present: trim = media box, 0 mm bleed. This is the exact print-ready file the shop already runs, with one city's details and one placed portrait.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (one portrait + what reads as eight tidy lines):
- Top ~45% of the card: a placed PORTRAIT PHOTOGRAPH (portrait crop) of that city's host in the 2025 file. This is the picture well the per-row image binds into this year.
- CITY: the city name as a heading, measured serif, large, Slate #33404B.
- VENUE: the venue name, plain grotesque, medium, Ink Near-Black #191F24, set on ONE line at a fixed width.
- ADDRESS: the street address, plain grotesque, small, Cool Grey #8A929A.
- DATE: the event date, plain grotesque, medium, Ink Near-Black #191F24.
- HOST_NAME: the host name, plain grotesque, medium, Ink Near-Black #191F24.
- HOST_TITLE: the host title, plain grotesque, small, Cool Grey #8A929A.
- SEAT_TIER: the seat-tier line, plain grotesque small caps, Amber #E0A02C.
- STANDING_LINE: the fixed doors / register line, plain grotesque, small, Cool Grey #8A929A.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The CITY, VENUE, ADDRESS, DATE, HOST_NAME, HOST_TITLE, SEAT_TIER and STANDING_LINE are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame (city \n venue \n address \n date \n host name \n host title \n seat tier \n standing line), NOT eight addressable frames. Eight fields landing in one flow is a different mapping problem from eight fields in eight frames: there is no per-field frame to map to and the whole strategy has to move to offsets inside one story.
- The portrait sits in its own rectangular GRAPHIC FRAME. This IS a genuine picture well, so the per-row VENUE photograph CAN be bound through the image column — but it must be bound per row or every one of the eleven cards ships the same picture.
- When the mapping readout (textContent) is taken off that story, the SEAT_TIER run is SILENTLY DROPPED while its trailing line break is KEPT, so the returned string still reads as a well-formed, complete block. Every character offset AFTER the seat-tier line is therefore short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those wrong offsets and prepare reports completed successfully, so the STANDING_LINE (mapped by offset after the seat tier) silently never lands and the SEAT_TIER line itself is absent from every merged card — on a card whose whole job is to tell each city its seat tier and how to register. The true story text must be reconstructed from the prepared document's own content runs, every offset recomputed against that string, and every placeholder re-confirmed in a freshly exported structure rather than trusted from the success message.
- FIXED DETAIL MEASURE: the venue line is set on one line at a fixed width, so a venue name that runs long does not spill or reflow — it simply stops rendering and truncates at the trim edge, which reads like a deliberate design choice on a proof.
- NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a bleed-safe press-ready delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): CITY | VENUE | ADDRESS | DATE | HOST_NAME | HOST_TITLE | SEAT_TIER | STANDING_LINE | @IMAGE (per-row venue photo).

Colours: Paper White #F6F4EF ground, Slate #33404B city heading, Ink Near-Black #191F24 venue / date / host name, Cool Grey #8A929A address / host title / standing line, Amber #E0A02C seat-tier line.

On the panel is a compound brand lockup: on the left a HEXRING glyph — a hexagonal ring with a fine enclosed inner counter (an open hexagonal hole through the centre, the ring stroke fairly thin relative to the hole) — and to its right the wordmark NORVANT in quiet clean small-caps grotesque letters, everything cut or printed in one deep slate-grey ink (hex #33404B) on the brushed-metal panel. assets.content:
NORVANT — LAUNCH COPY (approved, legal-cleared, do not edit the three claims)

THE RELEASE
The March release is called Throughline. It is the work the whole company has been building toward. When you name the release in the cut or on a card it is "Throughline" — not "the Throughline update", not "Throughline 1.0".

THE THREE CLEARED CLAIMS (verbatim — legal signed these off; they cannot be reworded, shortened or paraphrased)
1. "Norvant connects to the systems your finance and operations teams already run, without a rebuild."
2. "Every automation keeps a full audit trail your controller can export."
3. "Most teams have their first workflow live in an afternoon, without writing code."
Elise says all three of these in the take, in her own words around them. If a claim did not survive the tightening into the explainer, it does not go into a caption either. Do not invent a fourth claim and do not soften these into a benefit line.

SIX PRESS-FRAME CAPTIONS (one per frame, in this order; plain, no exclamation marks)
PF1. "Elise on why Norvant exists."
PF2. "The Throughline workspace, running."
PF3. "An audit trail, exported in one click."
PF4. "Setup, start to first workflow."
PF5. "Finance and operations, one queue."
PF6. "Elise, closing."

STANDING EVENT-CARD WORDING (the same line on every city card, set below that city's own details)
"Doors 6:00pm. Talk at 6:30pm. Seating is limited — register at norvant.com/march."

WHO WE ARE / VOICE
Norvant is workflow automation for finance and operations teams. Seats are one hundred and forty dollars a month and nothing gets bought without three people signing off, so everything has to read like it was made by people who know what they are doing. Plain, specific, confident without selling. Slate and amber, quiet, no stock smiles. Tell us plainly what you could not do and why — we would rather know now.

A NOTE ON THE MARK
The mark is a hexring glyph beside the wordmark NORVANT, cut in slate. The only place it still exists at any size is the sign on the reception wall; the original files went with the agency. Recover it off the sign — do not redraw it into a font and do not regenerate it. The ring is a ring: it has to still read as a ring at the size it prints on a card and reversed on the amber ground, not a filled hexagon.

A NOTE ON THE TYPE
One quiet type system: a plain neutral face for detail and body, a measured companion for headings. Nothing expressive, nothing decorative. This typography reaches the announcement set. The printed city cards carry the printer's own faces from last year's file, so say so in the note rather than pretending one system covers both.
